text:
Recent work supports separating recency sensitivity from sequence understanding. [Oh and Cho (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) find that excessive recency bias can hurt recommendation accuracy. [Spotify’s 2026 capacity study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) shows that independent item-transition contributions with recency weighting can rival Transformers on several benchmarks; those datasets differ from the four target categories. [Temporal-aware contrastive learning (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-8994/17/10/1634) also warns that random augmentation can disrupt sequential semantics. Thus, sensitivity to shuffled histories alone does not establish useful temporal reasoning.

Suggested diagnostic design: compare equal-count recent, oldest, and random deletions within each user; shuffle earlier interactions while preserving the last item, then separately shuffle the entire history. Keep candidate sets, padding conventions, and inference mode fixed. Include unchanged-history controls and simple last-item, order-invariant, and recency-weighted scoring baselines. For repeated interests, define recurrence using observed item IDs or title/description similarity, then match control deletions on count and position; report exact repeats separately from semantic recurrence. Measure paired changes in validation HR@10, target rank, top-10 overlap, and encoder-feature similarity. Compare deletion with position-preserving masking only where masking is supported, since compaction changes positional inputs.

For uncertainty, resample users within each category, preserve original/perturbed pairing, and recompute the four-category macro-average difference; report 95% bootstrap intervals and variability across shuffle seeds. [SciPy’s bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) describes paired index resampling. These are proposed model-sensitivity probes: ranking changes reveal dependence under constructed inputs, not causal proof of current intent or observed psychological traits.
